speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your neck swelling, could you tell me how long it has been present and if it is painful to the touch? Also, have you noticed any recent fever, weight loss, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, is this swelling firm and fixed to the underlying structures, or does it feel soft and mobile? Additionally, has the area changed in color, or do you notice any visible skin changes like dimpling or ulceration?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, I am concerned this may be a metastatic lesion, so I need to check for other signs of recurrence. Do you have any unintentional weight loss, loss of appetite, or changes in your bowel habits since the swelling appeared? Also, are you experiencing any shortness of breath or persistent cough?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, I need to rule out metastasis, so I will order a CT scan of the neck and chest along with a biopsy of the swelling. REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck_and_Chest. REQUEST TEST: Neck_Swelling_Biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan and biopsy were normal, I need to clarify if this swelling is soft, fluctuant, or firm, and if it has increased in size over the last few weeks. Do you recall any history of trauma to that area, or have you noticed the swelling changing size with your posture or activity?

speaker: Patient
text: Overall healthy appearance, no other complaints or symptoms noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the imaging and biopsy were normal, I need to determine if this is a benign cystic lesion like a lipoma or epidermoid cyst. Does the swelling feel soft and doughy, or is it distinctively firm, and do you feel any warmth in the area?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal biopsy and CT results, is this swelling soft and compressible like a lipoma, or does it feel firm and fixed to the skin like an epidermoid cyst? Also, does the mass change in size when you lie down or sit up?

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI_Neck. Given the normal biopsy and CT, an MRI will help us differentiate between a lipoma and other soft tissue masses that might be missed on CT.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI and biopsy results suggest this is likely a benign lipoma, given your history and the lack of other symptoms. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lipoma of the posterior neck.
